stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A red laser passes through a narrow slit of width $a$ and lands on a distant screen. Instead of a single spot, you get a wide central bright band flanked by dimmer side fringes — this is diffraction. Sweep all three sliders (slit $a$, wavelength $\lambda$, distance $D$) to see how each one shapes the pattern.
stages.concept: Central fringe width: $L = \dfrac{2\,\lambda\,D}{a}$. Half-angular width: $\theta \approx \dfrac{\lambda}{a}$. Narrower slit or longer wavelength → wider pattern. Diffraction is 'appreciable' when $\lambda / a$ is not small.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Match the ghost pattern on the right side of the screen: its width $L^{*}$ AND its color $\lambda^{*}$ must both match. Since $L = 2\lambda D / a$ has three unknowns for one width, many $(a, D)$ pairs work — but only one $\lambda$.
stages.concept: $L^{*} = \dfrac{2\,\lambda^{*}\,D}{a}\ \Rightarrow\ a = \dfrac{2\,\lambda^{*}\,D}{L^{*}}$. Pick $\lambda$ first (color-matches the ghost), then tune $a$ and $D$ to hit $L^{*}$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The intensity pattern is hidden — the screen just shows two target dots at $\pm d^{*}$. Pick $a$, $\lambda$, $D$ so that the first dark fringes land exactly on the dots (i.e. $L/2 = d^{*}$). Peek briefly reveals the true pattern.
stages.concept: First-minimum position: $\dfrac{L}{2} = \dfrac{\lambda\,D}{a} = d^{*}$. So $\dfrac{\lambda\,D}{a} = d^{*}$ — many triples work, pick one and check the grey marker aligns.

labels.tip1: move each slider across at least half its range
labels.tip2: match both the width L and the color λ of the ghost
labels.tip3: align the first dark fringe (L/2) with the target dots

1.1: Try halving a — the central band should roughly double in width.
1.2: Switch λ from red (633) toward violet (400) — the pattern narrows.
1.3: Doubling D also doubles L (linear scaling with screen distance).

2.1: Read the ghost color: red ≈ 633 nm, green ≈ 532 nm, blue ≈ 450 nm.
2.2: Once λ matches, tune a alone — L = 2λD/a means small a = wide L.
2.3: If you can't reach L*, adjust D too. Solve: a = 2λD / L*.

3.1: The dots are at ±d* from center. You need L/2 = d*, so L = 2d*.
3.2: Rearrange: a = λD / d*. Pick any λ and D, then compute a.
3.3: Peek to see the pattern for 1.5 s. If it's centered and its first zero hits the dots, you're done.
